tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

content.text:
I've read `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/progress.md`. I haven't changed, audited or looked up anything else. Here's how I understand this chat.

**What this chat covers:** the Terms + Accept moment, built as real screens. According to `progress.md`, that's:

- **S3, choose amount.** Tiers go in ascending order with equal visual weight. Nothing is pre-selected, and the blocked tier stays visible with its reason.
- **S4, terms + accept.** It's a separate screen, so the full cost fits without scrolling. The accept button names the amount, and its second line names the repayment and date. The collection permission is its own unticked `Choice`. Accept stays enabled; tapping it without the permission shows a neutral inline message.
- **The receipt after accepting.** You kept it because the moment isn't finished until the user knows it worked.
- **The reduced-payout screen.** Possibly in scope; it's a full screen in the accept path.

**How we'd work:** one screen per request. For each one I write a short plan and wait for your OK, then build it, run `npm run build` and `npm run check`, check it in the running app and commit. Every number and date comes from `salaryAdvance.js`, and every money string comes from `formatAmount`.

**Open items that touch these screens.** They're yours to decide when we reach them, not now:

1. **Where the lasting record of the agreement lives.** The receipt has to say where.
2. **Whether the payout lands on the day it's accepted.** The module assumes it, but your read doesn't say so yet. It shapes the receipt copy.
3. **Button loading colour.** It currently keeps the brand colour, and you haven't confirmed that.
4. **Whether `Choice` requires a `disabledReason`.** This matters for the blocked tier on S3.
5. **The frame plus padding is 892px tall.** On a short laptop screen the page scrolls, which affects how "cost visible without scrolling" gets checked on S4.

**Two things to settle before we start:**

- **What "moments A and B" means.** In Chat 2 you scoped depth in two places: terms + accept, and the late path. Is A Terms + Accept and B the late path, with only A in this chat? Or do both A and B sit inside Terms + Accept?
- **Where to start.** `progress.md` lists your read's loose ends and the reviewer state switcher before the screens. I'd go straight to S3, unless you want the switcher first so each state can be reached from beside the frame.

Tell me which, and I'll bring the plan for that first screen.

# NovaPay Salary Advance — Product Reference

A one-page reference so you can focus on design, not on inventing a lending model. Treat these as the rules of the product. Where something isn't specified, make a reasonable assumption and state it.

> NovaPay is a fictional digital wallet used for this exercise. The numbers below are illustrative but internally consistent — design as if they're real.

## What it is

A short-term **salary advance**: a small amount of cash to help a salaried user bridge to their next payday. Short tenor, fixed fee, single repayment pulled on payday.

## Loan tiers

| Tier | Amount (PKR) |
|------|--------------|
| 1 | 5,000 |
| 2 | 10,000 |
| 3 | 15,000 |

A user's offered limit is the highest tier they qualify for. They can take any amount up to that limit (in the tiers above). Requesting more than the offered limit is **not allowed** — that's one of the hard moments you'll design for.

## Cost & repayment

- **Fixed fee** per advance: **3% of the amount disbursed**, charged once (not monthly interest). Example: a Rs 10,000 advance costs Rs 300, so the user repays **Rs 10,300**.
- **Tenor:** repaid in full on the user's **next payday** (assume ~2–4 weeks out; the exact date is known at offer time).
- **Total cost of credit** (amount + fee) and the **repayment date** must be clear at the moment of decision. (See "Trust rules.")
- A "haircut" can apply: the amount actually disbursed may be lower than requested if risk checks warrant it.

## Decisions

- **Approved** — an offer is available; the user can accept.
- **Declined** — no offer. Reasons we surface internally: `credit_score`, `income_unverified`, `other`. How (and how honestly) a decline is communicated to the user is a design decision.
- Income may or may not be **verified** at application (bank statement / payslip). Unverified income is a common decline reason.

## Repayment outcomes (post-disbursement)

- **on_time** — repaid on or before the due date.
- **late** — repaid after the due date (we track days late).
- **default** — 30+ days past due. A user with an active late/overdue advance is a sensitive state to design for (reminders, what they see, tone).

## Trust matters most here

NovaPay operates in a market where predatory digital-lending apps have harmed users and drawn regulatory action — and lending is the highest-trust moment in the whole app. How you earn (or lose) that trust is the heart of this exercise: what you show, when you show it, and how you handle the moments that don't go well. We're deliberately not giving you a checklist — those calls are yours to make and defend.

## Glossary (mirrors the dataset fields, for context)

`applied_amount` · `disbursed_amount` (may be < applied) · `decision` (approved/denied) · `denial_reason` · `repayment_status` (on_time/late/default) · `days_late` · `income_verified` · `income_source` (salaried/freelance).

1	# My Problem Understanding
2	The salary advance was shipped fast and it shows at the hard moments: telling someone what an advance will cost, that they've been declined, or that a repayment is coming due. It converts fine, but the manager doesn't want to scale something that feels predatory. My job is to make those moments honest, even where that costs some conversion.
3	
4	> v1 of this read was written by me without AI. This version (v2) was rewritten with the help of AI after an AI critique; I edited it, and every call in it is mine. The critique and my responses are in the table at the end.
5	
6	## What I'm working from
7	I haven't seen the live flow. The starter has one home card ("You may qualify for a NovaPay salary advance" / "See your offer"), and its button only shows a TODO toast. So this section is evidence plus the risks I'm designing against, not things I observed.
8	
9	**Evidence**
10	- **The manager's message:** "converts fine but feels off at the edges: the terms, the decline screen, the repayment reminders." Success is being measured by conversion.
11	- **The brief:** shipped fast; the hard moments are cost, decline, and a repayment coming due.
12	- **The product reference:**
13	  - The payout can be lower than requested.
14	  - Decline reasons are internal codes, and how honestly to explain them is "a design decision".
15	  - Total cost and the due date "must be clear at the moment of decision".
16	- **The starter card:** "See your **offer**" claims an offer already exists. ("You may qualify" is only a hedge.) The card is shown to everyone, right under a low balance (Rs 4,250).
17	
18	**Risks I'm designing against**
19	- **Entry:** the card implies an offer exists and nudges people when their balance is low. It should reflect the user's real situation (eligible, needs verification, already has an advance, late).
20	- **Cost:** a fee shown only as a % is hard to judge. Each tier should show the fee in rupees, the total and the due date. A tier above the limit should explain why, not throw an error.
21	- **Accept:** a vague action ("Continue") taking out a loan, consent bundled or pre-ticked, nothing to show what was agreed afterwards. Also everything after the tap: processing, a double tap, a network failure, and a reduced payout arriving after the user has already said yes.
22	- **Repayment:** reminders that pressure, notifications that expose the debt, collection that drains the wallet, and consequences explained too late.
23	
24	## What's working
25	- It converts, so people want it. That doesn't prove they understand it.
26	- A fixed one-time fee is simpler to understand than interest that grows. (from the product reference, not observed)
27	- Repayment is tied to payday, with a single repayment. (from the product reference, not observed)
28	- The three tiers are simple choices; no slider, no free-text amount.
29	- Amounts are formatted consistently through one component.
30	
31	## My position on conversion
32	I accept lower conversion in these places, on purpose:
33	1. Full cost and due date on the same screen as the accept button.
34	2. A separate, explicit permission to collect from the wallet.
35	3. Verification shown up front, so unverified users don't start an application.
36	4. No default amount, and no urgency.
37	
38	## Why someone ends up late
39	Repayment is collected on payday once salary has landed, at a fixed time (6pm). The reminder before the due date says exactly when. A borrower is only late if:
40	- **payroll was delayed** (not their fault),
41	- **they lost their job** (not their fault),
42	- **their salary moved to a bank account**, or
43	- **they spent the money before collection.**
44	
45	The first two aren't the user's fault, and that's why the late experience should be calm and practical, never accusing.
46	
47	**Due date vs salary arriving:** Days late are counted from 28 Jul, as the product reference says, and shown truthfully. The tone is calm from day 1. If payroll is delayed, the user can tell us and reminders pause.
48	
49	# Predatory behaviors we want to avoid
50	
51	**Entry**
52	- Claiming an offer exists before eligibility is known.
53	- Defaulting to the largest amount.
54	- Countdown timers or "offer expires".
55	- Asking for access to contacts, photos or SMS in exchange for a bigger limit. (Income documents to check affordability are fine. Personal data harvesting never is.)
56	
57	**Cost**
58	- Showing the fee after commitment.
59	- Hiding when and from where repayment is taken.
60	- Calling it "no interest". 3% over 21 days is about 52% a year.
61	
62	**Accept**
63	- Pre-ticked consent.
64	- A vague button that takes the loan.
65	- Bundling permission to collect from the wallet into "I agree".
66	- No record of what was agreed.
67	
68	**Decline**
69	- A no with no reason.
70	- Making people keep re-applying. Instead we re-check on a stated date, and they never need to apply again.
71	
72	**Late**
73	- Contacting family, contacts or the employer.
74	- Public shaming.
75	- Debt details on the lock screen.
76	- Constant notifications.
77	- Freezing the wallet.
78	- Paying a fee to push the date back (rollovers).
79	- Taking the whole salary the moment it lands.
80	- Threatening language.
81	
82	## Principles (each one can fail a screen)
83	1. **The number you tap is the number you owe.** On the screen with the accept button, the amount received, the fee in rupees, the total and the due date are all visible without scrolling or tapping. The button names the amount and the date.
84	2. **Know before you ask.** No user reaches a "no" that could have been known before they applied. Only the credit check happens at application.
85	3. **Smaller is never harder.** Tiers in ascending order, nothing pre-selected, the same visual weight for each, no timers, no expiry.
86	4. **Late is a situation, not a character flaw.**
87	   - At most 2 reminders a week.
88	   - None between 10pm and 8am.
89	   - No amount, "loan" or "overdue" on the lock screen.
90	   - Never sent to anyone but the borrower.
91	   - Red only on the event that failed (e.g. "We couldn't collect on 28 Jul"), never on the person's status card or the late screen. Their status uses the attention colour.
92	   - Attention colour (provisional): the existing amber ramp, only as a soft background with dark text (body text neutral-900 on accent-50; accent-600 only for the short status label). Never a solid fill, never on headlines, no alarm icons. The system audit confirms it.
93	5. **Their wallet stays theirs.** The advance is shown separately from their own money. Collection only ever takes what's owed, attempted once each time salary lands, never on a daily loop (whether retries are allowed is an open question). The wallet is never frozen. 
94	
95	## A moment that shouldn't exist
96	**"Declined: income unverified."**
97	- Assuming verification status is known before anyone applies (see Assumptions), the home card can show verification as a step to complete first, instead of letting the user apply and then declining them: "Verify your salary to unlock an advance", with the steps.
98	- No application is made, so no decline is recorded.
99	- **Counter-argument I accept:** using wallet data to pre-screen needs the user's consent, and the backend's decline reason would need to change. It's a product change, not just copy.
100	
101	## Scope
102	Built as separate states the reviewer can jump to, so the depth goes into two places.
103	
104	**In depth: terms + accept**
105	- Tiers with the fee in rupees, the total and the date. The over-limit tier is shown blocked, with the reason.
106	- What happens if it's late, in one line, with details behind an expandable section. Default consequences are stated here, at accept (placeholder copy until compliance confirms).

# My Problem Understanding
The salary advance was shipped fast and it shows at the hard moments: telling someone what an advance will cost, that they've been declined, or that a repayment is coming due. It converts fine, but the manager doesn't want to scale something that feels predatory. My job is to make those moments honest, even where that costs some conversion.

> v1 of this read was written by me without AI. This version (v2) was rewritten with the help of AI after an AI critique; I edited it, and every call in it is mine. The critique and my responses are in the table at the end.

## What I'm working from
I haven't seen the live flow. The starter has one home card ("You may qualify for a NovaPay salary advance" / "See your offer"), and its button only shows a TODO toast. So this section is evidence plus the risks I'm designing against, not things I observed.

**Evidence**
- **The manager's message:** "converts fine but feels off at the edges: the terms, the decline screen, the repayment reminders." Success is being measured by conversion.
- **The brief:** shipped fast; the hard moments are cost, decline, and a repayment coming due.
- **The product reference:**
  - The payout can be lower than requested.
  - Decline reasons are internal codes, and how honestly to explain them is "a design decision".
  - Total cost and the due date "must be clear at the moment of decision".
- **The starter card:** "See your **offer**" claims an offer already exists. ("You may qualify" is only a hedge.) The card is shown to everyone, right under a low balance (Rs 4,250).

**Risks I'm designing against**
- **Entry:** the card implies an offer exists and nudges people when their balance is low. It should reflect the user's real situation (eligible, needs verification, already has an advance, late).
- **Cost:** a fee shown only as a % is hard to judge. Each tier should show the fee in rupees, the total and the due date. A tier above the limit should explain why, not throw an error.
- **Accept:** a vague action ("Continue") taking out a loan, consent bundled or pre-ticked, nothing to show what was agreed afterwards. Also everything after the tap: processing, a double tap, a network failure, and a reduced payout arriving after the user has already said yes.
- **Repayment:** reminders that pressure, notifications that expose the debt, collection that drains the wallet, and consequences explained too late.

## What's working
- It converts, so people want it. That doesn't prove they understand it.
- A fixed one-time fee is simpler to understand than interest that grows. (from the product reference, not observed)
- Repayment is tied to payday, with a single repayment. (from the product reference, not observed)
- The three tiers are simple choices; no slider, no free-text amount.
- Amounts are formatted consistently through one component.

## My position on conversion
I accept lower conversion in these places, on purpose:
1. Full cost and due date on the same screen as the accept button.
2. A separate, explicit permission to collect from the wallet.
3. Verification shown up front, so unverified users don't start an application.
4. No default amount, and no urgency.

## Why someone ends up late
Repayment is collected on payday once salary has landed, at a fixed time (6pm). The reminder before the due date says exactly when. A borrower is only late if:
- **payroll was delayed** (not their fault),
- **they lost their job** (not their fault),
- **their salary moved to a bank account**, or
- **they spent the money before collection.**

The first two aren't the user's fault, and that's why the late experience should be calm and practical, never accusing.

**Due date vs salary arriving:** Days late are counted from 28 Jul, as the product reference says, and shown truthfully. The tone is calm from day 1. If payroll is delayed, the user can tell us and reminders pause.

# Predatory behaviors we want to avoid

**Entry**
- Claiming an offer exists before eligibility is known.
- Defaulting to the largest amount.
- Countdown timers or "offer expires".
- Asking for access to contacts, photos or SMS in exchange for a bigger limit. (Income documents to check affordability are fine. Personal data harvesting never is.)

**Cost**
- Showing the fee after commitment.
- Hiding when and from where repayment is taken.
- Calling it "no interest". 3% over 21 days is about 52% a year.

**Accept**
- Pre-ticked consent.
- A vague button that takes the loan.
- Bundling permission to collect from the wallet into "I agree".
- No record of what was agreed.

**Decline**
- A no with no reason.
- Making people keep re-applying. Instead we re-check on a stated date, and they never need to apply again.

**Late**
- Contacting family, contacts or the employer.
- Public shaming.
- Debt details on the lock screen.
- Constant notifications.
- Freezing the wallet.
- Paying a fee to push the date back (rollovers).
- Taking the whole salary the moment it lands.
- Threatening language.

## Principles (each one can fail a screen)
1. **The number you tap is the number you owe.** On the screen with the accept button, the amount received, the fee in rupees, the total and the due date are all visible without scrolling or tapping. The button names the amount and the date.
2. **Know before you ask.** No user reaches a "no" that could have been known before they applied. Only the credit check happens at application.
3. **Smaller is never harder.** Tiers in ascending order, nothing pre-selected, the same visual weight for each, no timers, no expiry.
4. **Late is a situation, not a character flaw.**
   - At most 2 reminders a week.
   - None between 10pm and 8am.
   - No amount, "loan" or "overdue" on the lock screen.
   - Never sent to anyone but the borrower.
   - Red only on the event that failed (e.g. "We couldn't collect on 28 Jul"), never on the person's status card or the late screen. Their status uses the attention colour.
   - Attention colour (provisional): the existing amber ramp, only as a soft background with dark text (body text neutral-900 on accent-50; accent-600 only for the short status label). Never a solid fill, never on headlines, no alarm icons. The system audit confirms it.
5. **Their wallet stays theirs.** The advance is shown separately from their own money. Collection only ever takes what's owed, attempted once each time salary lands, never on a daily loop (whether retries are allowed is an open question). The wallet is never frozen. 

## A moment that shouldn't exist
**"Declined: income unverified."**
- Assuming verification status is known before anyone applies (see Assumptions), the home card can show verification as a step to complete first, instead of letting the user apply and then declining them: "Verify your salary to unlock an advance", with the steps.
- No application is made, so no decline is recorded.
- **Counter-argument I accept:** using wallet data to pre-screen needs the user's consent, and the backend's decline reason would need to change. It's a product change, not just copy.

content.text:
**S3: choose an amount**

Everything below uses Persona A on 7 Jul. Each value comes from `getOffer(PERSONAS.A, "2026-07-07")`. None of it is code yet.

### Layout and copy, top to bottom

**1. AppBar**
- Title: **"Salary advance"**
- Back (‹) goes to home (S1). This is the first way out.

**2. Card (default tone): how repayment works.** It sits above the choice, so the rules come before the decision.
- Heading (body, semibold): **"How repayment works"**
- Body (body, neutral-900):
  - "You repay everything on **28 Jul**, your next payday, in 21 days."
  - "At **6pm**, once your salary has landed, we collect it from your NovaPay wallet."
  - "The fee is **3%** of the amount you receive. It's charged once and added to what you repay."
- Sources:
  - `28 Jul` comes from `formatDate(offer.due_date)`.
  - `21` comes from `offer.days_until_due`.
  - `6pm` comes from `formatTime(COLLECTION_TIME)`.
  - `3%` comes from `FEE_PERCENT`.

**3. Fieldset in one white Card, with neutral-200 dividers between the rows**
- Legend (title): **"How much do you want to borrow?"**
- Hint under the legend (caption, neutral-700): "You can borrow up to Rs 10,000."
- Inline message slot. It's empty until someone taps the primary button with nothing chosen.
- Three `Choice` radios with the same `name`, all unchecked:

| Label | Description / reason (caption, neutral-700) |
|---|---|
| **Rs 5,000** | "Fee Rs 150 · Repay Rs 5,150 on 28 Jul" |
| **Rs 10,000** | "Fee Rs 300 · Repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul" |
| **Rs 15,000** (disabled) | "Above your limit of Rs 10,000." **[PLACEHOLDER]** "Your limit is based on your salary and how you use NovaPay." |

- The per-row line matches the S4 button's second line ("Repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul"), so the number someone picks here is the number they see again on the accept screen.
- Rs 15,000 shows no fee or total, because the module returns `null` for both. We show the reason instead and never invent a figure.

**4. Inline message (neutral, not red)**
- Copy: "Choose an amount to continue."
- It goes in the slot under the legend hint: body text, neutral-900, `role="status"`, no icon.
- Focus moves to the first radio.
- The message clears as soon as an amount is chosen.

**5. Sticky action area**
- Primary (lg): **"Review terms"**, with the second line "Nothing is borrowed yet". It stays enabled and goes to S4 with `getTerms(A, chosen, today)`.
- Secondary (lg): **"Back to home"**. This is the second way out, with the same weight as the primary button.

It fits easily: about 560px of content in an 844px frame, with no scrolling.

### Copy that states policy

- **The limit's basis is a placeholder.** The product reference only says the limit is "the highest tier they qualify for". If you'd rather not include a placeholder, the reason can be just "Above your limit of Rs 10,000.", which is factual.
- **No copy about raising the limit.** You rejected "the limit grows after on-time repayments", so the reason gives no hint of it.
- **The repayment card's claims are all in your Assumptions or the product reference:** 6pm once salary lands, from the wallet, a 3% fee charged once.

### Decisions I need from you

1. **Wallet balance.** I've left Rs 4,250 off this screen. It's on home, and showing it next to the amounts could push people towards borrowing more. Do you want it here?
2. **Collection time.** `getOffer` doesn't return the collection time, so the screen would read the `COLLECTION_TIME` constant. The alternative is adding `collection_time` to `getOffer`'s output. That's a small module change.
3. **The disabled radio looks greyed.** The browser greys a disabled native radio's circle, whatever we do. The label and reason stay neutral-700, but the control itself reads as greyed out. Changing that would be a `Choice` change, so it's your call.
4. **The "Nothing is borrowed yet" line.** It's true and lowers pressure, but you can cut it.
5. **Persona B.** Persona B never reaches this screen because they need verification first. If it's ever rendered for B, I'd send them to home rather than show an empty list.

message.content:
Critique this screen three ways: (1) as a regulator looking for misleading disclosure, (2) as a first-time borrower with low financial literacy reading it on a small Android phone, (3) as a screen-reader user. Only list problems; don't fix them.

this is for the choose an amount

content.text:
Here's the critique of S3 (choose an amount) as built in `b50c6eb`. It covers problems only, with the most serious first in each section. I worked from the code and the frame at 390px. I didn't test it on a real Android phone or with a real screen reader, so anything that depends on those is marked **unverified**.

## 1. A regulator looking for misleading disclosure

1. **There's no annual rate.** "3% … charged once" over 21 days is about 52% a year. Showing only a flat percentage and rupee fee makes it look cheap, and nothing on the screen lets someone compare it with other credit.
2. **The screen never says this is credit.** "Salary advance", "borrow" and "fee" never become "loan" or "credit". A regulator could read "advance" as a way to make it sound like early access to your own salary.
3. **The repayment figures are stated as certain, but they aren't.** "Repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul" appears before any risk check, and your own rules allow a reduced payout. The screen never says the amount can be lower than chosen.
4. **"Of the amount you receive" hints at the reduced payout without explaining it.** It suggests the amount received could differ from the amount chosen, but never says how or when.
5. **Collection is stated as a fact before consent.** "We collect the full amount from your NovaPay wallet" reads as a condition already agreed. The permission doesn't come until S4.
6. **Nothing covers what happens if salary doesn't land.** "Once your salary has landed" covers the case that works. Whatever happens otherwise is left out of the moment someone picks an amount.
7. **The blocked Rs 15,000 can work as an anchor.** A visible amount someone can't have can make the Rs 10,000 limit feel like a step towards more, and so encourage borrowing up to it.
8. **"Nothing is borrowed yet" sits on the commit path.** Putting reassurance on the primary button could be seen as lowering resistance at the moment of decision.
9. **Some standard disclosures are missing:** who the lender is, a key facts statement, and any cancellation right. These are open questions in your read, but a regulator would see them as gaps, not as decisions made.
10. **The entry point still claims an offer.** The home button "See your offer" leads here before eligibility is shown, which is the pattern your read describes as predatory.

## 2. A first-time borrower with low financial literacy, on a small Android phone

1. **The most important numbers are the smallest text.** The amount received is bold body text, but what they'll owe ("Repay Rs 10,300") is a 13px caption in grey. The page visually reverses principle 1.
2. **Three paragraphs come before the question.** On a 360×640 phone the repayment card can fill most of the first screen, so the amounts sit below the fold. The fixed 390×844 frame never shows this. **Unverified.**
3. **Android's large text setting isn't tested.** At larger font sizes, the title, the button's second line and the tier lines will wrap and push the options down further. **Unverified.**
4. **"3% of the amount you receive" is a percentage.** "Receive" also raises the question of whether they'll get less than they chose.
5. **Some words assume financial confidence:** "salary has landed", "collect", "Review terms", "limit". "We collect" may not register as "money will be taken from my wallet automatically".
6. **"The full amount" is abstract in the card.** No figure appears there. They have to connect it to the tier line below.
7. **The middle dot in "Fee Rs 150 · Repay Rs 5,150 on 28 Jul" may not read as a separator.** The line can run together as one string of numbers.
8. **The Rs 15,000 circle looks greyed out by the browser,** and tapping it does nothing. It can look broken or feel like a judgement, and "limit" is never explained.
9. **The inline message sits above the options.** Someone who taps the bottom button on a short screen may not see the message if the top of the card is scrolled away. Focus moving to Rs 5,000 may scroll it back into view, but that isn't guaranteed. **Unverified.**
10. **It's English only.** Urdu is an open question in your read, and that matters most for this reader.

## 3. A screen-reader user

1. **The screen change is silent.** Going from home to S3 doesn't move focus, and the page title stays "NovaKit Lite". A TalkBack or NVDA user isn't told they're on a new screen.
2. **Keyboard users never meet Rs 15,000.** Disabled radios are skipped by Tab and the arrow keys, so they never hear that the tier exists or why it's blocked. The reason is only reachable by reading through the page.
3. **The "Choose an amount" message can be missed.** It's announced politely through `role="status"` at the same moment focus jumps to Rs 5,000. The focus announcement can talk over it. On a second tap the text is unchanged, so it isn't announced again.
4. **The hint may not be read.** "You can borrow up to Rs 10,000." is linked to the fieldset with `aria-describedby`, which screen readers support inconsistently on a group. Some will never say it.
5. **The question isn't a heading.** "How much do you want to borrow?" is a legend. Someone jumping by headings hears "Salary advance" and "How repayment works", then nothing for the choice itself.
6. **The repayment terms are outside the form.** A user jumping between form controls hears the amounts and fees but skips the card with 6pm, the wallet and the fee rule.
7. **The primary button's name may run together.** It could be read as "Review terms Nothing is borrowed yet", with no pause. The browser tool showed both buttons with no name at all, which needs checking with a real screen reader. **Unverified.**
8. **The radios' names also need checking.** The browser tool listed them as "5000", "10000" and "15000", not "Rs 5,000". If that's what a screen reader announces, the currency is lost. **Unverified.**
9. **Short forms may read badly:** "Rs" may be read letter by letter, "Jul" as a word, "6pm" as "6 p m", and the middle dot as "dot" or nothing.
10. **Two "back" controls with different names go to the same place.** The AppBar's "Back" doesn't say where it goes, while "Back to home" does. That's minor, but they're inconsistent.

The two items I'd check first with real tools are 3.7 and 3.8, the button and radio names. If either is true, the accessible names lose the numbers this screen exists to show.

Showing the tier above the limit, with a plain reason, is the over-limit moment the brief asks me to design. Hiding it would be less transparent, not more. It sits last in ascending order, has the same visual weight, shows no fee or total, and has no “unlock” or “grow your limit” language, so nothing invites reaching for it. Rejected. The card comes before the choices in reading order, so a screen-reader user reading the page hears the terms first. Moving terms into the form would make the controls harder to use without adding anything. The full terms are repeated on S4, where the commitment happens. Add them to the Pushback list in progress.md.

content.text:
## SR7 and SR8: the accessible names

**The browser pane's tree isn't reliable here.** It reported the radios as "5000", "10000" and "15000" and gave both buttons no name. Its tree is built from the DOM: it uses the radio's `value` and ignores `aria-labelledby`. So that was a measuring problem, not a real one.

**The real names come from Edge's own accessibility tree.** I read it in headless Edge over the DevTools protocol. The script is in the scratchpad, and nothing was installed.

| Element | Name | Description | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| radio | "Rs 5,000" | "Fee Rs 150 · Repay Rs 5,150 on 28 Jul" | SR8 passes |
| radio | "Rs 10,000" | "Fee Rs 300 · Repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul" | SR8 passes |
| radio | "Rs 15,000" | "Above your limit of Rs 10,000." | It's disabled and **not focusable**, which confirms SR2 |
| button | "Review terms Nothing is borrowed yet" | none | **SR7 confirmed:** a space but no stop, so it's read as one run-on phrase |
| button | "Back to home" | none | OK |
| group (fieldset) | "How much do you want to borrow?" | "You can borrow up to Rs 10,000." | Chromium does read the hint. SR4 may only affect other screen readers, but moving the hint into the legend fixes it everywhere anyway |

The rejected points are now in `progress.md` → Pushback (`de6bfe0`).

## R1 (annual rate): my call is to leave it off S3

- S3 has just been shortened for small phones.
- "About 52% a year" needs an explanation longer than any line on the card: it's a flat fee, it doesn't compound, and the term is 21 days.
- Whether the fee counts as interest, and how an annual rate should be stated, is on your "want to know" list. Any comparison line would therefore be stating policy.
- If it goes anywhere, it goes on S4, where cost is the subject, as placeholder copy.

## Revised S3, top to bottom

**Shell (every screen, SR1)**
- Each screen sets the page title. This one is "Choose an amount: NovaPay".
- On a screen change, focus moves to the screen's `h1`. It doesn't move on the first page load.

**AppBar**
- Title: "Salary advance". See decision 1 below.
- Back: `aria-label="Back to home"` (SR10).

**Card**
- Heading: **"How it works"**
- "A salary advance is a short-term loan. You repay it all on **28 Jul**, your next payday (in 21 days)."
- "If you accept, we take the full amount from your NovaPay wallet automatically at **6pm**, once your salary arrives. The fee is charged once."
- What moved to S4: the 3% and "added to what you repay".

**Fieldset**
- The legend holds both lines (SR4/SR5): the heading **"How much do you want to borrow?"**, then "You can borrow up to Rs 10,000."
- The tiers, unselected and in ascending order:

| Line 1: label, body semibold | Line 2: body semibold, neutral-900 (B1) | Line 3: caption, neutral-700 |
|---|---|---|
| Rs 5,000 | You repay Rs 5,150 on 28 Jul | Fee Rs 150 |
| Rs 10,000 | You repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul | Fee Rs 300 |
| Rs 15,000 | none | Above your limit of Rs 10,000. |

- Screen readers hear, for example: "Rs 10,000, radio, You repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul. Fee Rs 300." The middle dot is gone (B7).
- **The final-amount line goes right under the tiers** (R3/R4), in body text, neutral-700: "We'll confirm the final amount before you accept. It may be lower than you choose."
- **Rs 15,000** uses `aria-disabled` (SR2):
  - It's focusable and announced as unavailable, with its reason.
  - It can't be selected by tap or arrow key.
  - Its circle is dimmed, matching the greyed native look you accepted earlier.

**Sticky action area**
- The inline message sits above the primary button (B9): "Choose an amount to continue." It's body text, neutral-900, no icon.
  - It replaces the slot under the legend.
  - Every tap clears it and sets it again, so it's announced each time (SR3).
  - Focus moves to the fieldset, which reads its name and hint.
  - It clears as soon as an amount is chosen.
- Primary (lg): **"Review terms"**, second line "Nothing is borrowed yet". It will be announced as "Review terms. Nothing is borrowed yet." (SR7).
- Secondary (lg): **"Back to home"**

**Home (R10):** "See your offer" becomes **"See amounts and costs"**.

**After the build:** I'll check the layout at 360×640 by overriding the frame's size in the browser only. The allow-list doesn't change. I'll re-read Edge's tree to confirm every name and description above.

## Component changes, each to be logged in `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`

1. **Choice:** `aria-disabled` instead of `disabled`, with the selection blocked and the circle dimmed (SR2).
2. **Button:** a full stop for screen readers only, between the label and the second line (SR7). S4's accept button benefits too: "Accept Rs 10,000. Repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul."
3. **AppBar:**
   - an optional `backLabel` (default "Back") for SR10,
   - the `h1` gets `tabIndex={-1}`, so the shell can focus it (SR1).

## Decisions I need from you

1. **The AppBar title.** If S3 and S4 both say "Salary advance", SR1 announces the same heading on both screens, so a screen-reader user can't tell them apart. I'd use "Choose an amount" here and a specific title on S4, matching the page title.
2. **Where the "You repay" line's styling lives.** I'd style it inside the description I pass to `Choice`, with no component change, since only S3 needs it. The alternative is a new `Choice` prop.
3. **B4 and B8 weren't triaged.**
   - B4, the percentage: this version resolves it by dropping the 3% from S3.
   - B8, the circle that looks broken: it's partly covered by SR2. Tapping Rs 15,000 still gives no feedback beyond its reason.

   Tell me if either needs more.

content.text:
I tried each draft in the running S3 at 360×640, in a background tab. I only swapped the card's text in the page, so no source files changed. The current card is 226px tall, so Rs 5,000's fee line is cut off and Rs 10,000 is below the fold.

## What fits

With no heading, the card fits in **4 lines (122px)**. Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000 are then fully visible, with 8px to spare below Rs 10,000's fee line. Any 5-line version cuts Rs 10,000's fee line by 14px, and keeping the "How it works" heading cuts it by 22px.

**Rs 15,000 can't fit above the fold through copy alone.** It needs about 66px more, which is a whole row. It's reached by scrolling, and the limit is already above the fold in the hint: "You can borrow up to Rs 10,000."

## Option A (recommended)

> A short-term loan with a **3%** fee, charged once. If you accept, we take the full amount from your NovaPay wallet automatically at **6pm** on **28 Jul**, once your salary arrives.

- **It keeps:** "loan" (R2), the 3% (B4), "If you accept" and "automatically" (R5, B6), your own edit "the full amount", the NovaPay wallet, 6pm, 28 Jul, and "once your salary arrives".
- **It drops:**
  - the "How it works" heading,
  - "next payday (in 21 days)",
  - the words "salary advance". The AppBar now says "Choose an amount", so this screen would no longer use the product's name.

## Option B (keeps your R2 sentence)

> A salary advance is a short-term loan with a **3%** fee, charged once. If you accept, we take it from your wallet automatically at **6pm** on payday, once your salary arrives.

- **It keeps:** your exact R2 wording and the product's name.
- **To fit in 4 lines it gives up:**
  - "the full amount" becomes "it", which undoes your earlier edit,
  - "NovaPay wallet" becomes "wallet",
  - "28 Jul" becomes "payday". Each tier still says "on 28 Jul".

## Why I recommend A

Both drafts tell people it's a loan. A also says exactly what is taken, from which wallet, and when. Those are the facts someone needs before choosing, and B makes each of them vaguer.

## What changes besides the copy

- **The card loses its heading,** so a screen reader moves straight from the "Choose an amount" heading to the question.
- **Nothing else moves.** At 390×844 the card simply gets shorter.

How it works

content.text:
**S4: terms + accept.** Everything below uses Persona A on 7 Jul. Every value comes from `getTerms(PERSONAS.A, 10000, "2026-07-07")`, and money and dates go through `formatAmount`, `formatDate` and `formatTime`. None of it is code yet.

## Layout and copy, top to bottom

**1. AppBar**
- Title: **"Review and accept"**. The page title is "Review and accept: NovaPay".
- Back: `backLabel="Back to amounts"`. It returns to S3 with Rs 10,000 still chosen.

**2. Cost summary card.** This is principle 1, so it sits at the top.
- Heading (body, semibold): **"Your advance"**
- Three `ListRow`s with `wrap`:

| Title | Subtitle (caption) | Trailing |
|---|---|---|
| You get | Paid into your NovaPay wallet | **Rs 10,000** |
| Fee | 3%, charged once | **Rs 300** |
| **You repay on 28 Jul** | At 6pm from your NovaPay wallet, once your salary arrives | **Rs 10,300** |

- The date is in the third row's title, not its grey subtitle. That's the B1 lesson from S3.
- Last line of the card (caption, neutral-700): "If we can only pay a lower amount, we'll show you the new terms and ask you again before paying anything." This comes from your Assumptions: a reduced payout needs fresh consent.

**3. What if it isn't collected (card)**
- One line (body): "If we can't take it on 28 Jul, we'll tell you that evening and try again when your salary next arrives."
- Native `<details>`, with the summary **"What happens if it's late"**:
  - "Days late are counted from 28 Jul."
  - "You can pay some or all of it yourself at any time."
  - "If your salary is delayed, tell us and we'll pause reminders. We'll still send the notice on 20 Aug."
  - "Reminders come at most twice a week, never between 10pm and 8am, and only to you."
  - "We won't freeze your wallet."
  - "If it's still unpaid on 27 Aug, the advance is in default. New advances are paused and automatic collection stops."
  - **Placeholder:** "Other consequences of default are being confirmed."
  - **Placeholder:** "Whether a late fee applies is being confirmed." (Decision 2 below.)

**4. Permission card.** A `Choice` checkbox, unticked.
- Label: "I allow NovaPay to take Rs 10,300 from my NovaPay wallet automatically at 6pm on 28 Jul once my salary arrives, or when it arrives after that."
- Description: "This permission ends when the advance is repaid, or on 27 Aug at the latest. It only applies when your salary arrives, never to other money in your wallet."
- **Inline message**, under the checkbox and only shown after Accept is tapped without the tick:
  - Copy: "To accept, tick the box to give this permission."
  - It's body text, neutral-900, no icon, `role="status"`, cleared and set again on every tap.
  - Focus moves to the checkbox.
  - The message clears when the box is ticked.

**5. Sticky action area**
- Primary (lg): **"Accept Rs 10,000"**, with the second line "Repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul". It stays enabled. Screen readers hear "Accept Rs 10,000. Repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul".
- Below it, two secondary (md) buttons side by side, with equal weight: **"Change amount"** (back to S3, Rs 10,000 kept) and **"Back to home"** (resets the amount).
- Laying two buttons side by side is a layout choice, not a Button change.

**Space check (an estimate, which I'll measure after the build).**
- The footer is about 150px. The cost card ends at about 300px.
- It fits without scrolling in the 390×844 frame, and should also fit at 360×640, where about 434px of content is visible.
- The permission card will need scrolling on small phones. The cost won't.

## Annual rate: my recommendation is to show it, labelled as a placeholder

- Your read already states the arithmetic: 3% over 21 days is about 52% a year.
- Hiding it on the commitment screen is the "flat fee looks cheap" pattern a regulator would flag (R1).
- Placement: one caption line under the Fee row: "For comparison, this fee works out to about 52% a year." Its wording is labelled as a placeholder until compliance says how a yearly rate must be stated.
- It needs a module field, `annual_rate_equivalent`, calculated in the module (fee ÷ amount × 365 ÷ days) and covered by the check. Screens never calculate it.

## Decisions I need from you

1. **The annual rate:** show it as above, or leave it out?
2. **The late-fee placeholder line.** Late fees are "pushing for, not confirmed", so I can't say there are none and can't invent one. Keep the labelled placeholder line, or say nothing?
3. **When the money lands.** "Paid into your NovaPay wallet" avoids saying "today", because "the payout lands when accepted" is still an open question, not one of your Assumptions. Do you want it to say "today"?
4. **S3's copy may contradict this flow.** S3 says "We'll confirm the final amount before you accept." Your read says a reduced payout can arrive after the tap, with fresh consent (S7). A more accurate S3 line would be: "If we can only pay less, we'll ask you again before paying anything." Should I change S3 when we build this?
5. **Where Accept goes.** Until the receipt (S5) is built, a ticked Accept would call `acceptTerms`, which is idempotent, and open a labelled placeholder screen, the same pattern as S3's "Review terms". Is that OK?
6. **Missing terms.** If `getTerms` returns `null` (no amount chosen, over the limit, or Persona B), the screen sends them to S3, or to home for Persona B. Is that OK?

file.content:
- Panel as an alias of Card (`e1171a8`).
- **Phone frame:** fixed at 390×844, `main` scrolls, a sticky action area, a neutral-50 screen background (`8199d1e`), and the desktop scrollbar hidden (`9f0367c`).
- **The allow-list is down to 6:** three for the phone frame, the backdrop, and two for the frozen copy. Every starter-debt entry is gone.
- `npm run build` and `npm run check` pass after every commit. Nothing is pushed.

## Decisions

### Chat 1: project setup

- **Flattened the zip's `novakit-lite/` folder into the repo root** so the repo is the project itself, with no extra folder level.
- **Kept the zip out of the repo with `.git/info/exclude`, not `.gitignore`,** so the only change to the starter's `.gitignore` is the `_inputs/` line that was asked for.
- **Kept `brief.md` inside `_inputs/`** so it's covered by the same ignore rule and the brief is never published.
- **Did not run `npm audit fix`,** even though the install reported 14 vulnerabilities (4 moderate, 10 high). Fixing them would change the starter's lockfile.
- **Wrote `brief.md` as Markdown that follows the PDF's layout.** The boxed sections became blockquotes, the page footers were dropped, and the sentence split across pages 1 and 2 was joined.
- **Used a Stop hook rather than UserPromptSubmit for the prompt log.** Stop doesn't fire on an interrupt, so cancelled prompts stay out of the log.
- **Gave each logged prompt and session a hidden ID marker.** This means a prompt is never logged twice, and sessions stay grouped even when they alternate.
- **Wrote the hook in Node** because Python isn't installed on this machine.

### Chat 2: critique of my read, and rails

- **Scope is depth in two places:** terms + accept, and the late path (reminder before the due date → not collected on payday → late → notice before default). The home card (eligible vs needs verification) and home after accepting are thin. The credit decline, default screen, successful repayment and viewing the advance later are cut.
- **"Declined: income unverified" shouldn't exist.** Verification becomes a step on the home card before anyone applies. This rests on an assumption that verification status is known before applying.
- **Kept the receipt after accepting:** the accept moment isn't finished until the user knows it worked.
- **Kept the reminder before the due date:** it's the one chance to prevent two of the causes of lateness.
- **No grace rule:** days late are counted from the due date and shown truthfully.

input.prompt:
You are reviewing one screen of a React prototype for inconsistencies. This is a READ-ONLY task: do not create, edit or delete any file, do not run git commands that change anything (no add/commit/checkout/stash), and do not install anything. You may run `npm run build` and `npm run check` from the project root if useful, and read any file.

Project root: D:\Frontend\Side Projects\Finance App (a NovaPay salary-advance case study built on a small design system, "NovaKit Lite").

## What to review
S4, the "terms + accept" screen: `src/screens/ReviewAccept.jsx`. Also the code it depends on or that was changed for it:
- `src/App.jsx` (PhoneFrame shell with `sheet` slot, routing, `accept()`, ReceiptPlaceholder)
- `src/novakit/BottomSheet.jsx` (just rewritten as an accessible dialog)
- `src/novakit/Choice.jsx`, `src/novakit/Button.jsx`, `src/novakit/ListRow.jsx`, `src/novakit/AppBar.jsx`, `src/novakit/Card.jsx`
- `src/advance/salaryAdvance.js` (the single source of truth for money and dates; `getTerms`, `acceptTerms`, constants)
- `src/screens/ChooseAmount.jsx` (S3) only where S4 must be consistent with it (copy, patterns, the lower-payout line)

Uncommitted changes exist; `git diff` shows the latest S4 work against the last commit.

## The context to check against
Read all of these fully:
- `CLAUDE.md` (working rules: one source of truth, design system rules, Trust and copy rules)
- `PRODUCT_REFERENCE.md` (product rules)
- `docs/00-my-read.md` (the owner's read: principles 1–5, Predatory behaviours, Scope, Assumptions, What I'd want to know)
- `docs/progress.md` (decisions so far, open questions, Pushback)
- `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` (component/token change log)
- `docs/01-system-audit.md` (audit decisions, "My decision" column)

## Decisions the owner made in chat that the docs may not reflect yet
Treat these as the owner's current intent, NOT as bugs. But DO report every place where a doc, a rule or another screen now contradicts them, because that's an inconsistency to resolve.
1. No annual rate is shown anywhere: the fee is a fixed 3% of the amount, charged once.
2. S4 has no late-fee line and no "other consequences are being confirmed" line.
3. The default line ("If it's still unpaid on 27 Aug, the advance is in default. New advances are paused and automatic collection stops.") has NO placeholder label.
4. "You get" row subtitle is "Paid into your NovaPay wallet" (deliberately no timing).
5. The late consequences moved from a native <details> into a BottomSheet (owner asked for a bottom drawer).
6. The checkbox text was shortened so it doesn't repeat the amounts/date shown in "Your advance": label "I allow NovaPay to take the repayment above automatically.", description "This ends automatically when it's repaid, or on 27 Aug at the latest."
7. The "tick the box" message shows in the sticky action area above the Accept button; focus still moves to the checkbox.
8. "Change amount" and "Back to home" are two equal secondary buttons side by side.
9. Accept goes to a labelled receipt placeholder until S5 is built.
10. S3's line was changed to "If we can only pay a lower amount, we'll ask you again before paying anything."

## What to look for
- Copy that states a policy not backed by PRODUCT_REFERENCE.md or the Assumptions in 00-my-read.md (invented policy), or that contradicts them.
- Trust and copy rule breaks in CLAUDE.md (pre-ticked, permission not its own checkbox or not stating when it ends, cost not visible without scrolling, "no interest", "never" about fees, urgency/blame wording, red on status, "Rs 0" or guessed numbers, unlabelled placeholder policy copy).
- One-source-of-truth breaks: any money, date, time or rule computed or hard-coded in a screen instead of read from the module (e.g. "that evening", "twice", 3%, 6pm, dates).
- Design system breaks: hex or arbitrary values, new components/tokens not logged in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md, log entries that don't match the code.
- Accessibility problems in what was built (dialog focus/escape/trap, status announcements, names, headings, focus order) — reason from the code.
- Behaviour bugs: state that doesn't reset, controls that do nothing, edge cases (terms null, double accept, sheet open while navigating), React issues (hooks, effects, StrictMode double effects).
- Inconsistencies between S4 and S3 (wording for the same thing, patterns, button sizes, message placement).
- Docs now stale because of the decisions above (progress.md, DESIGN_SYSTEM.md, 01-system-audit.md, 00-my-read.md, CLAUDE.md).

## Output
Return a findings list, most important first. For each finding give:
- severity: High (breaks a stated rule or is a real bug) / Medium (inconsistency the owner must decide) / Low (polish or stale doc)
- where: file:line
- what's inconsistent, quoting the exact text on both sides (the code/copy and the rule or doc it conflicts with)
- whether it's a code problem or a doc that needs updating
Do not propose large rewrites; one-line suggested resolution per finding at most. Separately list anything you checked that is consistent and worth confirming (briefly). Be precise and don't pad: if something isn't really an inconsistency, leave it out.

The review agent re-checked S4 against `CLAUDE.md`, the product reference, your read, `progress.md`, the audit and the design system log. Build and check pass. I confirmed the main points myself in the code and the module, and nothing has been changed.

## Things on S4 that are wrong now

1. **The retry promise is mostly untrue.** S4 says: "If we can't take it on 28 Jul, we'll tell you that evening and try again when your salary next arrives."
   - The module only retries when salary lands.
   - If salary came in short, the balance dropped, or salary moved to a bank, the next salary is 28 Aug. That's after default on 27 Aug, and after the permission has ended.
   - So the promise only holds when salary is delayed.
   - Whether retries are allowed is still an open question in your read.
2. **The checkbox is never actually checked by the module.** `App.jsx:83` always calls `acceptTerms` with `permission_granted: true`, whatever the screen holds, so the module's own guard can never trigger.
3. **"That evening" is a time hard-coded in the screen.** It only holds because collection is at 6pm. It should come from the module, as "at 6pm".
4. **The sheet doesn't fully block the screen behind it.**
   - If focus drops off the sheet, Tab can reach the buttons behind the backdrop.
   - Some screen readers can still move through the page behind.
   - Setting the rest of the frame to `inert` while the sheet is open fixes both. The design system log currently claims more than the code does.
5. **"What happens if it's late" is a 22px tap target.** Everywhere else uses at least 44px.
6. **I mislabelled the receipt as "S5".** In the audit and the module's scenarios, S5 is Processing and **S8 is the receipt**. I wrote it wrong in an `App.jsx` comment and in the `progress.md` I committed.

## Decisions for you

7. **The shorter checkbox no longer covers the later attempt.** "The repayment above" points to the 28 Jul, 6pm row, but item 1 promises to try again later. The checkbox also no longer says "never other money in your wallet", which your Assumptions call for.
8. **S3 and S4 word the lower-payout line differently, at different sizes.**
   - S3: "…we'll ask you again before paying anything." (body text)
   - S4: "…we'll show you the new terms and ask you again before paying anything." (caption)
9. **The default line has no placeholder label.** `CLAUDE.md`, your Assumptions, and the audit's S4 and S13 rows all still say default consequences are labelled placeholders. This is already listed as open in `progress.md`.
10. **"Back to home" is a large button on S3 and a medium one on S4.** On S4 the same destination also has two names: the AppBar's "Back to amounts" and the button "Change amount".

## Docs that are out of date (no code change needed)

- `progress.md`:
  - still says S4's late details are a native `<details>` and that BottomSheet is unused,
  - still says the "tick the box" message sits at the checkbox,
  - still asks about an annualised rate,
  - says "3% of the amount borrowed", where the product reference says "of the amount paid out".
- The audit says the same about the details element and the message.
- Your read still quotes the old, long permission wording (line 107). I'll leave that to you.

## Lower priority

- The default line reads the permission's end date instead of `terms.default_date`. They're the same today but mean different things.
- The receipt placeholder's heading is "Salary advance" rather than the screen's name.
- Home still hard-codes the balance and the transactions. This predates S4.

I'd fix items 1–6 in code now. Item 1 needs your wording, though. My suggestion is "If we can't take it on 28 Jul, we'll tell you at 6pm. If your salary is late, we'll try again when it arrives." Items 7–10 are yours to decide. Nothing is committed.

65	### Chat 4: S3 (choose an amount) and S4 (terms + accept)
66	
67	- **Module:** `getOffer` now returns `collection_time`, so S3 can say "6pm" without reaching for a constant. The check was changed first and failed until the field existed (`41e94a1`).
68	- **S3, first version** (`b50c6eb`): the tiers as unselected radios, the over-limit reason, a neutral inline message, "Review terms" wired to a labelled placeholder, and home's button wired to S3.
69	- **Critique of S3 three ways** (regulator, low-literacy borrower on a small Android phone, screen-reader user), then my triage: fix, reject, defer. The rejections are in Pushback below (`de6bfe0`).
70	- **The accessible names were checked in Edge's real accessibility tree** (headless Edge over the DevTools protocol, nothing installed). The browser pane's tree was wrong: it named radios by their `value` and gave buttons no name.
71	- **NovaKit changes, logged in `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`** (`5c2e023`):
72	  - Choice uses `aria-disabled`, so a blocked option stays focusable and its reason is heard,
73	  - Button adds a stop between its two lines for screen readers,
74	  - AppBar gets `backLabel`, and its `h1` can take focus,
75	  - Toast gets a `neutral` variant.
76	- **S3 revised after triage, and the shell** (`c4f284e`):
77	  - new copy and hierarchy: "You repay Rs X on 28 Jul" is the strong line and the fee is secondary,
78	  - the question and limit hint are the legend,
79	  - the "choose an amount" message sits next to the button and is announced on every tap,
80	  - tapping Rs 15,000 shows a neutral toast,
81	  - home's button says "See amounts and costs",
82	  - every screen sets the page title and moves focus to its `h1` on a screen change,
83	  - overlays sit above the action area, so a toast never hides the way out.

  - Toast gets a `neutral` variant.

  - new copy and hierarchy: "You repay Rs X on 28 Jul" is the strong line and the fee is secondary,
